collection.runs_note: The full run is collected in four batches of 10 industries because of storage limits in n8n; each batch's tables are exported to CSV and then removed from n8n. Every prompt is sent once to each engine.
collection.attempts: up to 3 per answer (failed requests retried up to two times)

brand_lists.base: the 40 industry lists drafted from the pilot answers and reviewed by a person (668 brands)
brand_lists.additions: brands in full-run answers that are not on the base list are drafted the same way and reviewed by a person before step 6
brand_lists.alias_rules: aliases of one or two characters and number-only aliases are dropped; aliases that are everyday English words (first 8,000 entries of a pinned common-word list) or acronyms match only case-sensitively

questions.answer_singles_out: Does `answer` itself single out one or more brands as its recommendation, at the beginning, at the end, or as its suggestion for a purpose, for example "the top choices are X and Y", "I recommend X", "I would look into X or Y first", "for this goal I would suggest X and Y" or "the best choice is X"? Answer no if it only gives a list of brands, including a list of "best for ..." entries or one labelled "best overall", without singling any out.
questions.brand_singled_out: Is {brand} one of the brands that `answer` itself singles out as its recommendation, for example "the top choices are X and Y", "I recommend X", "I would look into X or Y first", "for this goal I would suggest X and Y" or "the best choice is X"? Answer no if {brand} only appears as an entry in a list, even one labelled "best for ..." or "best overall", or as an alternative.
questions.brand_offered_as_option: Does `answer` recommend {brand} to the reader as an option to choose, rather than only mentioning it?

recommendations.rule: If the answer singles out at least one brand, only the singled-out brands are recommended; otherwise every brand offered as an option is recommended.

page_owner.order: own_site, retailer, review_platform, social_media, other, competitor, publisher (first match wins)

fetch.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

fallback.via: Oxylabs realtime API, universal source, geo_location United States
fallback.when: blocked (HTTP error or challenge page), fewer than 150 words of text, or redirected to another language version
tries: plain request (JavaScript rendering for pages that came back without text)
the same with a mobile user agent
the other of plain and rendered

left_out: Google search and shopping result links
pages with no HTML after all tries

page_type.question: What kind of page is `page`, by its format (not by who owns it)?

labels.listicle: Listicle: a list of several options, ranked or not, such as "best X", "top 10 X" or "X alternatives".
labels.comparison: Comparison: two or three named options compared side by side, such as "X vs Y".
labels.review: Review: an assessment of one product.
labels.article: Article: an informational article that does not list or rank options, such as a how-to, an explainer or a buying guide.
labels.news: News: a report on recent events, including press releases.
labels.homepage: Homepage: the front page of a website.
labels.product_page: Product page: a page about one product, plan or service.
labels.pricing_page: Pricing page: the plans and prices of one company.
labels.category_page: Category page: a store page listing many products of one kind.
labels.directory: Directory: a listing of many companies with a profile for each, such as G2, Clutch or Yelp.
labels.forum: Forum: a discussion thread, such as Reddit, Quora or a community.
labels.documentation: Documentation: a help center or product documentation page.

criticism.question: Does `page` criticize {brand}: does it state a drawback, weakness, complaint or con of {brand}, or say who {brand} does not suit? Answer no for plain facts such as prices, fees, plan limits, what a plan does not include, availability or fine print, unless the page presents them as a downside of {brand}.

ranks.what: backlink-based ranks, 0 to 1,000, for each measured page, its domain and each brand's own domain

analysis.too_little_data: a model is not fitted when fewer than 10 pages are cited more than once, when a yes-or-no measure has fewer than 10 pages on either side or no page cited more than once on one side, or when the fit does not converge
analysis.thesis_support: a measure that keeps its link after correction, in the same direction on at least three of the four engines

hand_checks.how: suggested marks from a second reader, confirmed or changed by a person
